sonnet.q1: It gets 401. Redis is not called and no counter changes. Unknown keys are not cached.
sonnet.q2: All of a customer's keys share one budget and one counter, so three keys together get the plan limit per minute (100 requests per fixed minute for Standard). Enterprise is NOT STATED (no limit set yet).
sonnet.q3: A 429 with a Retry-After header (no X-RateLimit headers). The backend never sees the request; it is not forwarded.
sonnet.q4: No. The count is not raised when denied, so a 429 uses no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The counter is raised before forwarding, so the request stays counted and the backend error goes back with X-RateLimit headers.
sonnet.q6: Fail open: the gateway forwards it to the backend anyway, with no X-RateLimit headers, and emits ratelimit_store_unavailable. The request may or may not have been counted.
sonnet.q7: Standard is 100 requests per minute. Enterprise has no limit set yet (Product has not chosen one; Enterprise cannot go live until it is).
sonnet.q8: In a shared Redis store, as a counter keyed rl:<customer ID>:<minute>. Old counts are removed by a 120 second TTL set on the first increment.
sonnet.q9: When the next fixed clock minute starts, a new window with a new counter key begins at zero. The old counter expires by TTL. Budget does not otherwise recover.
sonnet.q10: check_and_incr is a Lua script in Redis that reads the counter and adds 1 only if under the limit. Redis runs a script in one step, so two instances cannot both take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: Retry-After = 60 - (current Unix second mod 60), a whole number from 1 to 60: the seconds until the next clock minute starts.
sonnet.q12: Retry of the store: NOT STATED (the document describes no retry; it forwards the request). The client gets no X-RateLimit-* headers.
